mainTopic: Bringing offerings when unsure what was vowed: mixed loaves and wafers, why a מנחת נסכים is excluded, and the dispute over forgotten numbers of עשרונים.
overview: The amud opens with a suggestion for someone who vowed an oven-baked מנחה but forgot whether he said חלות or רקיקין: bring both together. The גמרא defends this using רבי שמעון. One קמיצה from either type counts for both, and the leftover oil goes to the כהנים either way. רב כהנא then asks why the forgetful person does not also worry about a מנחת נסכים. The גמרא answers with five differences that put the מנחת נסכים in a separate group. Next comes the משנה's case of someone who forgot how many עשרונים he promised. A ברייתא records that חכמים require one vessel of sixty, while רבי requires every amount from one to sixty separately. רב חסדא explains the dispute as being about bringing חולין into the עזרה. רבא says it is about mixing a חובה with a נדבה. אביי then challenges how the two handfuls in רבא's approach can be taken and burned, and his question about the order of burning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Taking the handful from one type for the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: if he brings loaves and wafers together, the קמיצה taken from the loaves would also count for the wafers, and the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and from wafers. But then he would be taking the handful from the loaves on behalf of the wafers, and from the wafers on behalf of the loaves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against the idea that the unsure person should bring a mix of חלות and רקיקין. The problem is that one קמיצה would be serving two different types of bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כהן takes a single handful from a mixed offering, he takes it from one type only. That handful then has to count for the other type too. This looks wrong, because each type seems to need its own קמיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick loaves, mixed with oil
Thin wafers, smeared with oil
Takes the handful (קְמִיצָה) from the מנחה to burn on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This step begins in the middle of a sentence. The word 'and from wafers' finishes the earlier idea of bringing the offering from both loaves and wafers together.

phrases.english: and from wafers; but then he takes a handful from the loaves for the wafers
and from the wafers for the loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge to the suggestion, made just before this point, that he bring a mixed offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the unsure person brings half חלות and half רקיקין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single קמיצה taken from one type cannot properly count for the other type.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: a handful from one type counts for both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון holds that if the handful came only from one type, it still counts for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have heard that רבי שמעון said: If he took the handful and what came up in his hand was from only one of the two types, it counts for both, and he has done his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting רבי שמעון. In his view, a קמיצה taken from only one type is valid for the whole offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון treats a half-loaves, half-wafers מנחה as one single offering. So it does not matter which part the handful comes from. The problem from step 1 therefore disappears, at least according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: From one type on behalf of both
He has fulfilled his obligation; the act is valid
And what came up in his hand

phrases.english: We have heard that Rabbi Shimon said:
If he took a handful and what came up in his hand
was from one type for both of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a known opinion (רבי שמעון) that makes the challenge go away
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each type needs its own קמיצה, so a mixed offering does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, one קמיצה from either type counts for both.

steps.title: The leftover oil problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: leftover oil is handled one way in a half-and-half offering and another way in an all-wafers offering, so the unsure person would not know what to do with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still the leftover oil! If he said half loaves and half wafers, the leftover oil goes back into the loaves. If he said all wafers, the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the mixed-offering suggestion, this time about the extra oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person does not know which type he vowed. If his vow was a half-and-half offering, the leftover oil must be mixed back into the loaves. If his vow was all wafers, the leftover oil belongs to the כהנים. With a mixed offering we cannot know which rule to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover oil remaining after the wafers are anointed
But there is still… (introduces a problem)
Is eaten by the כהנים

phrases.english: But there is the leftover oil!

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין אָמַר –
phrases.english: For if he said half loaves and half wafers,
he puts the leftover oil back into the loaves;
if he said all wafers,
the leftover oil is eaten by the priests.
phrases.notes: Since he does not remember which he said, we would not know whether the oil goes back into the loaves or to the כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after the קמיצה issue is answered, a second problem is raised about the oil.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion of bringing a mixed offering, even according to רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leftover oil is treated differently in the two possible vows, so a mixed offering leaves us unsure what to do with it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יהודה: the oil goes to the כהנים either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבי שמעון בן יהודה quoting רבי שמעון: wafers are anointed in a 'כי' shape and the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים, even in a half-and-half offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: He anoints them in the shape of a 'כי', and the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the oil problem with a ברייתא that reports רבי שמעון's view through רבי שמעון בן יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this view, the leftover oil of a half-and-half offering is not put back into the loaves. It goes to the כהנים, exactly as with an all-wafers offering. Both possible vows now lead to the same result, so the uncertainty causes no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: He anoints them (smears oil on the wafers)
In the shape of a 'כי', the Greek letter chi (X)
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: The mixed-offering suggestion works according to רבי שמעון. One קמיצה counts for both types, and the leftover oil goes to the כהנים whether the offering was half-and-half or all wafers.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both challenges are answered from opinions of רבי שמעון. This shows the suggestion holds up only within רבי שמעון's approach.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda, as it is taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
He anoints them in the shape of a chi,
phrases.notes: 'כי' here is the Greek letter chi, which looks like an X.

phrases.english: and the leftover oil is eaten by the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the oil challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a ברייתא with a view that makes both cases come out the same
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a half-and-half offering, the leftover oil goes back into the loaves, which is different from an all-wafers offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, the leftover oil is eaten by the כהנים in both cases, so the uncertainty does not matter.

steps.title: Shouldn't he also worry about a libation meal offering?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges: the forgetful person might have vowed a מנחת נסכים, because רבא says one may donate it any day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to רב אשי: But there is room to be unsure about a מנחת נסכים as well, since רבא said that a person may donate a מנחת נסכים every day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks why the person who forgot which מנחה he vowed brings only five types. Maybe he vowed a מנחת נסכים, which also exists as a donation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was that he brings the five standard types of מנחה to cover every possibility. רב כהנא uses רבא's ruling to show that a מנחת נסכים can also be a personal donation. If so, it should be a sixth possibility he has to cover.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering that comes together with the wine libations
To be unsure about it, to treat it as a possibility
Donates as a voluntary offering

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to Rav Ashi:
But there is room to be unsure about a libation meal offering,
phrases.notes: He means the person who vowed a specific מנחה and then forgot which one he vowed.

phrases.english: as Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְנַדֵּב אָדָם מִנְחַת נְסָכִים בְּכׇל יוֹם.
phrases.english: A person may donate a libation meal offering every day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge about the list of five מנחות that the forgetful person brings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the forgetful person brings only five types of מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא says a מנחת נסכים can be donated on its own. So it is another possible vow, and the list of five is missing it.

steps.title: First difference: offerings for an individual versus for the public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he is only unsure about offerings that come only for an individual. A מנחת נסכים can also come for the public, so it is not one of his options.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he is unsure (memory list: individual, due to, frankincense, with a לוג, takes a handful), it is about an offering that comes only for an individual. An offering that can come for the public is not something he is unsure about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a memory list of ways a מנחת נסכים is different. Then it explains the first difference: individual versus public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five types of מנחה he might have vowed come only from individuals. A מנחת נסכים also comes with public offerings, so it belongs to a different group. A person vowing 'a מנחה' did not have that kind in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory list of key words that helps you remember the points coming next
Because of, on account of
An individual
The public, the community

steps.confusionAlert: The words in brackets are not a ruling. They are just a memory list. Each word hints at one difference. Only the first difference (individual versus public) is explained in this step, and the other four are explained one by one in steps 7–10.

phrases.english: When he is unsure,
(Memory list: individual, due to, frankincense, with a log, takes a handful) –
phrases.notes: These words hint at the five differences the גמרא is about to list. Each one gets its own line in steps 6–10.

phrases.english: it is about one that comes due to an individual;

phrases.aramaic: בָּאָה בִּגְלַל צִיבּוּר – לָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: one that comes due to the public – he is not unsure about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge by showing that a מנחת נסכים is in a different group.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a מנחת נסכים can be donated, it should count as one of the possible vows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt only includes offerings that come only for an individual. A מנחת נסכים also comes for the public, so it is left out.

steps.title: Second difference: an offering on its own versus one that comes with an animal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second difference. He is only unsure about a מנחה that comes on its own, not one that comes because of an animal offering (זבח).
steps.simpleTranslation: When he is unsure, it is about an offering that comes on its own account. An offering that comes because of an animal offering is not something he is unsure about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list with the second difference. The five regular מנחות stand alone, but a מנחת נסכים normally comes along with a זבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the five regular מנחות is brought for its own sake. A מנחת נסכים is basically an add-on that goes with an animal offering. So it is not the kind of מנחה a person means when he vows one.

keyTerms.meaning: On its own account, for its own sake
An animal offering

phrases.english: When he is unsure –
it is about one that comes on its own account;

phrases.aramaic: בָּאָה בִּגְלַל זֶבַח – לָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: one that comes due to an animal offering – he is not unsure about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same answer with the second item from the memory list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A donated מנחת נסכים might be just like any other מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מנחת נסכים normally comes because of a זבח, unlike the five regular מנחות, so it is not one of his options.

steps.title: Third difference: frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The person is only unsure about a מנחה that needs לבונה. A מנחת נסכים needs no לבונה, so it is not one of his options.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he is unsure, it is about a מנחה that needs frankincense. A מנחה that does not need frankincense is not one of the things he is unsure about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more reason why a מנחת נסכים is not one of the forgetful person's options: it has no לבונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All five מנחות in the משנה are brought with לבונה. A מנחת נסכים is brought without לבונה. Since he knows he vowed a מנחה with לבונה, a מנחת נסכים does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Frankincense, put on a regular מנחה
Requires, needs
He is unsure about it

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ – טְעוּנָה לְבוֹנָה,
phrases.english: When he is unsure, it is about a מנחה that requires frankincense;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה לְבוֹנָה – לָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: one that does not require frankincense, he is not unsure about.
phrases.notes: The one without frankincense is the מנחת נסכים, the one רב כהנא brought up.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ – טְעוּנָה לְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third difference to the list started in steps 6 and 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is outside the doubt by listing a difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מנחת נסכים might be one of the forgetful person's options.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not, because it is brought without לבונה, unlike all the options he is unsure about.

steps.title: Fourth difference: amount of oil
steps.stepSummary: The person is only unsure about a מנחה brought with one לוג of oil. A מנחת נסכים has three לוגין or more, so it is not one of his options.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he is unsure, it is about a מנחה that comes with one לוג of oil. One that comes with three לוגין he is not unsure about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another difference: the amount of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the regular מנחות uses one לוג of oil. A מנחת נסכים uses at least three לוגין. Since he knows his מנחה was a one-לוג type, a מנחת נסכים is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of liquid; a regular מנחה uses one לוג of oil
Three לוגין, the smallest amount of oil for a מנחת נסכים

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ – בָּאָה בְּלוֹג,
phrases.english: When he is unsure, it is about a מנחה that comes with one log of oil;

phrases.aramaic: בָּאָה בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין – לָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: one that comes with three log, he is not unsure about.
phrases.notes: See במדבר 15:4–9. A quarter הין, which is three לוגין, is the smallest amount, and bigger animals get more.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ – בָּאָה בְּלוֹג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth difference to the same list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is outside the doubt by listing a difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מנחת נסכים might be one of his options.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not, because it uses three לוגין of oil, not one.

steps.title: Fifth difference: removing a handful
steps.stepSummary: The person is only unsure about a מנחה that needs קמיצה. A מנחת נסכים has no קמיצה, so it is not one of his options.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he is unsure, it is about a מנחה that needs a handful removed. One that does not need a handful removed he is not unsure about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a last difference: קמיצה. This finishes its answer to רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a regular מנחה, the כהן removes a handful (קמיצה) for the מזבח. A מנחת נסכים has no קמיצה. So for five reasons, a מנחת נסכים is not one of the things the forgetful person could have vowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a handful of the מנחה to burn on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: A מנחת נסכים is different from the regular מנחות in five ways: it can come for the public, it comes because of a זבח, it has no לבונה, it uses three לוגין of oil, and it has no קמיצה. So a forgetful person never has to bring one.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ – טְעוּנָה קְמִיצָה,
phrases.english: When he is unsure, it is about a מנחה that requires removal of a handful;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה קְמִיצָה – לָא קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: one that does not require removal of a handful, he is not unsure about.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא מִסְתַּפְּקָא לֵיהּ – טְעוּנָה קְמִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last difference and closes the answer to רב כהנא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is outside the doubt by listing a difference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מנחת נסכים might be one of his options.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is not, because it has no קמיצה.

steps.title: New case from the משנה: a מנחה of tenths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case of the משנה: someone who says 'I specified a מנחה of עשרונים' but forgot how many.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'I specified a meal offering of tenths.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on and quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up the discussion of this new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person knows he vowed a מנחה measured in עשרונים, but he forgot how many. The גמרא is about to discuss how he can bring enough to cover every possible number.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified, I said exactly
Tenths of an איפה, the measure of flour for a מנחה

phrases.english: "I specified a meal offering of tenths."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the forgotten type of מנחה and opens the משנה's next case, a forgotten number of עשרונים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה's case of a person who specified a מנחה of עשרונים and forgot the number. This sets up the discussion that follows.

steps.title: Forgot how many עשרונים he promised
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone promised a מנחה of a set number of עשרונים in one vessel but forgot the number. חכמים say he brings one מנחה of sixty. רבי says he brings sixty separate מנחות, from one to sixty, totaling 1,830 עשרונים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone says, 'I specified a מנחה and fixed it in one vessel of עשרונים, but I don't know what amount I specified,' he brings one מנחה of sixty עשרונים. This is the view of חכמים. רבי says he brings separate מנחות of every amount from one to sixty, which add up to 1,830 עשרונים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands the case of the משנה about a person who forgot how many עשרונים he promised. It records an argument between חכמים and רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sixty עשרונים is the most one vessel can hold for a single מנחה, so it covers anything he could have promised. חכמים think one big מנחה of sixty is enough, since his promise is inside it. רבי wants every possible amount brought as its own separate מנחה, so the exact amount he promised is brought by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: I specified (I said exactly what I was promising)
Tenths of an איפה, the unit used to measure flour for a מנחה
I fixed it to be brought in one vessel
The majority of the Sages, here arguing against רבי

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'I specified a meal offering,
and I fixed it in one vessel of tenths,
but I do not know what I specified' –
he brings a meal offering of sixty tenths,
phrases.notes: Sixty is the most one vessel can hold for a single מנחה, so it covers every possibility.

phrases.english: these are the words of the Sages.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: יָבִיא מְנָחוֹת שֶׁל עֶשְׂרוֹנִים
phrases.english: Rebbi says: he brings meal offerings of tenths
from one up to sixty,
phrases.notes: Sixty separate offerings: one of one tenth, one of two tenths, and so on up to sixty.

phrases.english: which come to one thousand eight hundred and thirty.
phrases.notes: 1 + 2 + 3 and so on up to 60 = 1,830 tenths.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פֵּירַשְׁתִּי מִנְחָה, וְקָבַעְתִּי בִּכְלִי אֶחָד שֶׁל עֶשְׂרוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the משנה case quoted in step 11 with a ברייתא that records a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: one מנחה of sixty עשרונים. רבי: sixty separate מנחות, from one to sixty (1,830 עשרונים).

steps.title: Forgot both the type of מנחה and the amount
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if he forgot both which type of מנחה and how many עשרונים, חכמים say five מנחות of sixty each (300). רבי says five types, each brought in every amount from one to sixty (9,150).
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'I specified, but I don't know what I specified, which type of מנחה I specified, or how many עשרונים I specified,' he brings five מנחות of sixty עשרונים each, which is 300. This is the view of חכמים. רבי says he brings the five types, each one in every amount from one to sixty, which adds up to 9,150.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a harder case: now he also forgot which of the five types of מנחה he promised. חכמים and רבי each apply their same approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are five types of מנחה, every option is multiplied by five. חכמים: five types × 60 = 300 עשרונים. רבי: five types × 1,830 = 9,150 עשרונים.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one of them (which type of מנחה)
The five types of מנחה brought by choice, such as סולת and מחבת
How many (the number of עשרונים)

phrases.english: 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified,
and which of them I specified,
phrases.notes: Which of the five types of מנחה listed earlier in the משנה.

phrases.english: and I do not know how much I specified' –
he brings five meal offerings
of sixty tenths each,
which are three hundred; these are the words of the Sages.
Rebbi says: he brings five meal offerings

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עֶשְׂרוֹנִים מֵאֶחָד וְעַד שִׁשִּׁים,
phrases.english: of sixty tenths, from one up to sixty,
phrases.notes: For each of the five types he brings sixty separate offerings, of one tenth up to sixty tenths.

phrases.english: which come to nine thousand one hundred and fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֵּירַשְׁתִּי וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה פֵּירַשְׁתִּי, וְאִי זוֹ מֵהֶן פֵּירַשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a harder case: the type of מנחה is also unknown.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: five מנחות of sixty each (300). רבי: five types × every amount from one to sixty (9,150).

steps.title: What are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic principle stands behind the argument between חכמים and רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea causes חכמים and רבי to argue. This question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us what each side rules but not why. The גמרא wants to find the underlying principle that explains why one big מנחה is enough for חכמים but not for רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root of an argument)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the dispute recorded in steps 12–13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides חכמים and רבי.

steps.title: רב חסדא: bringing חולין into the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the argument is whether one may bring חולין into the עזרה. רבי forbids it and חכמים permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: They disagree about whether one may bring חולין into the עזרה. רבי holds it is forbidden, and חכמים hold it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by pointing to one principle: may non-holy items be brought into the עזרה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he really promised less than sixty, the extra flour in the big מנחה is just חולין sitting in the עזרה. חכמים allow that, so one big מנחה works. רבי forbids it, so he must bring each amount separately, with nothing extra mixed in.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy items
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
To bring non-holy items into the עזרה

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוּתָּר לְהַכְנִיס חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: they disagree about whether it is permitted to bring non-sacred items into the Temple courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סָבַר: אָסוּר לְהַכְנִיס חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: Rebbi holds: it is forbidden to bring non-sacred items into the courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: מוּתָּר לְהַכְנִיס חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: it is permitted to bring non-sacred items into the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּמוּתָּר לְהַכְנִיס חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on whether חולין may be brought into the עזרה: רבי forbids, חכמים permit.

steps.title: רבא: mixing a חובה with a נדבה
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: everyone forbids bringing חולין into the עזרה. The argument is about whether one may mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees it is forbidden to bring חולין into the עזרה. Here they disagree about whether one may mix a חובה with a נדבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation of the same argument. He rejects the idea that it is about חולין in the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, both sides forbid חולין in the עזרה, so the extra flour cannot just be ordinary flour. Instead, the part he owes is a חובה and the extra is a נדבה, mixed together in one vessel. חכמים allow that mix, and רבי does not, so he requires each amount on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
An offering he is obligated to bring (here, what he promised)
A voluntary gift offering
To mix together

steps.whatToRemember: Two explanations of one dispute: רב חסדא says it depends on חולין in the עזרה. רבא says everyone forbids that, and it depends on mixing a חובה with a נדבה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing about the הלכה of the ברייתא. Both he and רב חסדא accept the rulings; they only disagree about the reason behind them.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָסוּר לְהַכְנִיס חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה,
phrases.english: everyone agrees it is forbidden to bring non-sacred items into the courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּמוּתָּר לְעָרֵב חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they disagree about whether it is permitted to mix an obligation with a gift offering.
phrases.notes: In the one big מנחה, the amount he owes is the obligation, and the extra would be a voluntary gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אָסוּר לְהַכְנִיס חוּלִּין לָעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 14 and rejects רב חסדא's basis.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Everyone forbids חולין in the עזרה; the dispute is whether a חובה may be mixed with a נדבה in one offering.

steps.title: How the Mixing Question Explains Each Side
steps.stepSummary: רבא spells out his explanation: חכמים permit mixing a חובה with a נדבה, and רבי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis hold it is permitted to mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one, and רבי holds it is forbidden to mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his answer by saying plainly which side holds what. חכמים allow mixing an obligation with a gift, and רבי does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים allow one vessel of sixty: whatever amount he really promised pays his נדר, and the extra is a נדבה mixed in with it. רבי forbids that mixing, so the person must bring every amount from one to sixty as its own separate מנחה. That is why רבי's total reaches 1,830 עשרונים.

keyTerms.meaning: To mix or combine together
An offering one is obligated to bring (here, to pay his נדר)
A voluntary gift offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, חכמים say one vessel of sixty is fine because a חובה may be mixed with a נדבה. רבי says each amount must be separate because mixing is forbidden.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: it is permitted
to mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one,
phrases.notes: In the one vessel of sixty, the part he really promised is the חובה and the rest is a gift.

phrases.english: and רבי holds: it is forbidden
to mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from step 16 by assigning each side its position.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What basic principle underlies the מחלוקת of חכמים and רבי?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים permit mixing חובה with נדבה; רבי forbids it.

steps.title: Wouldn't a Mixed Vessel Need Two Handfuls?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: if חכמים let one vessel hold both a חובה and a נדבה, shouldn't it need two separate קמיצות?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: According to the Rabbis, who say it is permitted to mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one, don't we need two handfuls?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a practical question about חכמים's view. A vessel holding two offerings would seem to need two handfuls taken from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each מנחה needs its own קומץ taken out and burned on the מזבח. If the one vessel really holds two offerings, a חובה and a נדבה, one handful should not be enough. אביי is asking how חכמים's single vessel can work in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Handfuls (plural of קֹמֶץ), the portion the כהן takes from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
We need / we require

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
According to the Rabbis, who say
it is permitted to mix an obligatory offering with a voluntary one,
don't we need two handfuls?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: לְרַבָּנַן דְּאָמְרִי מוּתָּר לְעָרֵב חוֹבָה בִּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבא's explanation of חכמים by asking how the קמיצה would work.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that חכמים allow one mixed vessel of חובה and נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two offerings in one vessel should need two קמיצות, so one handful would not be enough.

steps.title: The Priest Takes Two Handfuls
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the כהן does take two handfuls, one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: He takes a handful and then takes a handful again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא agrees that two handfuls are needed. He says the כהן simply takes one handful and then a second one from the same vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that two קמיצות are needed. He says the mixed vessel works because the כהן does two קמיצות from it. This sets up אביי's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: He takes a handful (does קמיצה)
And then again

phrases.english: He takes a handful and then takes a handful again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise and supplies a practical procedure
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single vessel can have only one קמיצה, so חכמים's view seems unworkable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהן takes two separate handfuls from the one vessel.

steps.title: But the Handfuls Come From the Wrong Parts
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: since everything is mixed, each handful contains flour from both the חובה and the נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is taking a handful from the obligation for the gift, and from the gift for the obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says two handfuls still don't solve the problem. Since everything is mixed, no handful comes purely from the part it is meant for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קומץ must come from the very מנחה it is for. In a mixed vessel, the handful meant for the חובה might really be taken from the נדבה flour, and the other way around. So the two handfuls seem to get crossed.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that (opens a challenge)
From the obligation on behalf of the gift

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not questioning the number of handfuls anymore. He accepts two handfuls; his problem now is that each one may be taken from the wrong part.

phrases.english: But he is taking a handful
from the obligation for the gift
and from the gift for the obligation!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא קָמֵיץ מֵחוֹבָה אַנְּדָבָה וּמִנְּדָבָה אַחוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that the כהן takes two handfuls
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a mixed vessel, each handful contains flour from both offerings, so neither handful comes only from its own offering.

steps.title: It Depends on the Priest's Hand
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the owner makes it depend on the כהן: whatever his hand takes first is the חובה, and what it takes at the end is the נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes it depend on the priest's intent, for he says: wherever the priest's hand reaches now shall be the obligation, and at the end, the gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the problem with a condition the owner makes ahead of time. The flour of the first handful counts as the חובה, and the flour of the second handful counts as the נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner leaves it open which flour belongs to which offering. That gets decided by where the כהן's hand reaches. Each handful then comes from the right part, and the problem of crossed handfuls is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes it depend (on something)
The intent or choice of the כהן
Now
At the end / afterward

steps.whatToRemember: According to חכמים, one vessel of sixty can hold both a חובה and a נדבה. The כהן takes two handfuls, and the owner's condition makes the first handful the חובה and the second the נדבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבא's explanation of the מחלוקת standing. חכמים's single vessel is practical once the owner sets this condition.

phrases.english: He makes it depend on the priest's intent,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person bringing the מנחה.

phrases.english: for he says: wherever
the priest's hand reaches now shall be the obligation,
and at the end, the gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a condition by the owner that decides which flour belongs to which offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each handful from a mixed vessel holds flour from both offerings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner's condition makes the flour of the first handful the חובה and the flour of the second the נדבה.

steps.title: If the gift handful is burned first, the obligation's remainder may be lacking
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks how the כהן burns the two handfuls. If he burns the נדבה handful first, maybe the whole mixture is really the חובה, and burning part of it leaves the חובה's שירים lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does he burn them? Suppose he burns the gift offering's handful first. Then how can he burn the obligation's handful? Maybe the whole thing is the obligation, and its remainder has now become lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי moves from taking the handfuls to burning them on the מזבח. He starts a two-sided challenge by testing the first possible order: burning the נדבה handful first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא already solved the problem of taking two handfuls. אביי says the order of burning still creates a problem. If the whole mixture might really be the חובה, then the second handful was really part of its שירים, so burning it makes those שירים lacking.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the handful on the מזבח
First
Perhaps, maybe
The remainder of a מנחה after the handful is taken; the כהנים eat it
Became lacking or reduced

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the mixture definitely is all חובה. He only says it might be. That doubt alone is enough to stop the כהן from burning the second handful.

phrases.english: And the burning, how does he burn?
If he burns the gift offering first,
then the obligation's handful, how can he burn it?
Perhaps all of it is the obligation,
and the remainder has become lacking.
phrases.notes: If it is all חובה, the second handful was really part of the remainder, so burning it shrank the remainder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's answer about taking the handfuls in Step 21, then challenges how the burning can be done.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's system of two separate handfuls from one mixed vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Burning the נדבה handful first could leave the חובה's שירים lacking, if the whole mixture is really חובה.

steps.title: The rule that lacking remainder blocks burning the handful
steps.stepSummary: אביי backs up his challenge with a known rule: if the שירים became lacking between קמיצה and הקטרה, the קומץ is not burned for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master said: if the remainder became lacking between taking the handful and burning it, one does not burn the handful on its account.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes an established rule to show why a lacking remainder is a real problem. This is the support for the challenge he just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this rule, a smaller remainder might seem harmless. The rule says that once the שירים are lacking before the burning, the קומץ can no longer be burned for that מנחה. So if the נדבה handful is burned first, the חובה's handful could not be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן taking a handful from the מנחה
Burning the handful on the מזבח
The handful itself that gets burned

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what turns אביי's doubt into a real halachic problem. Without it, the first horn of the challenge would have no force.

phrases.english: And the Master said:
A remainder that became lacking
between the taking of the handful and the burning,
one does not burn the handful on its account!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the halachic source that makes Step 22's concern a real problem.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that burning the נדבה handful first could invalidate the burning of the חובה's handful
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule taught by מר: if the שירים become lacking between קמיצה and הקטרה, the קומץ is not burned for them

steps.title: If the obligation handful is burned first, how can the gift handful be burned?
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns to the other possible order. If the כהן burns the חובה handful first, how can he then burn the נדבה handful?
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose he burns the obligation's handful first. Then how can he burn the gift offering's handful?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his two-sided challenge by testing the opposite order. Now both choices seem to cause a problem, and the גמרא needs an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first horn closed off burning the נדבה first. This second horn closes off burning the חובה first, so neither order seems to work. The גמרא explains the exact difficulty with this order on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him burn; a way of saying 'suppose he burns'
He burns
How?

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's challenge has two sides. Burning the נדבה handful first risks leaving the חובה's שירים lacking. Burning the חובה handful first leaves the question of how the נדבה handful can be burned. Neither order seems to work.

phrases.english: If he burns the obligation first,
then the gift offering's handful, how can he burn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second side of the challenge begun in Step 22, testing the opposite order of burning.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's system of two separate handfuls from one mixed vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the opposite order is also problematic, there seems to be no valid way to burn both handfuls.
